Fit a higher order multivariate Markov chain

Source: R/hommc.R
fitHighOrderMultivarMC.Rd

Fits the higher order multivariate Markov chain of Ching, Ng and Fung (2008) to several categorical sequences observed together: the next state of each sequence depends on the last order states of all the sequences, through a weighted sum of lag-specific transition matrices.

Usage

fitHighOrderMultivarMC(seqMat, order = 2, Norm = 2)

Arguments

seqMat

A matrix or data frame with one categorical sequence per column, all of the same length; numeric or factor values are taken as state labels (compared as character strings).

order

Order of the chain (default 2).

Norm

Norm used to estimate the weights (default 2): the weights minimize this norm of the difference between the state frequencies of each sequence and their image under the model, as in Ching et al. (2008). The minimization needs the suggested package Rsolnp.

Value

An hommc object. If Rsolnp is not available, NULL with a warning.

References

Ching, W.-K., Ng, M. K. and Fung, E. S. (2008). Higher-order multivariate Markov chains and their applications. Linear Algebra and its Applications 428(2-3), 492-507. doi:10.1016/j.laa.2007.05.021

See also

predictHommc() to simulate from the fit.

Other higher order chains: fitHigherOrder(), predictHommc()

Author

Giorgio Spedicato, Deepak Yadav

Examples

data <- matrix(c("2", "1", "3", "3", "4", "3", "2", "1", "3", "3", "2", "1",
                 "2", "4", "4", "4", "4", "2", "3", "3", "1", "4", "3", "3"),
               ncol = 2)
if (requireNamespace("Rsolnp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fitHighOrderMultivarMC(data, order = 2, Norm = 2)
}
